verses.text: But God did not forget Noah and all the wild animals and farm animals that were with him in the ark. God sent a wind over the earth, and the waters began to go down.
The springs of the deep and the floodgates of the sky were closed, and the rain stopped falling from the sky.
Little by little the water went down from the earth. After a hundred and fifty days the water had gone down,
and on the seventeenth day of the seventh month the ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat.
The waters kept going down until the tenth month. On the first day of the tenth month, the tops of the mountains could be seen.
After forty days, Noah opened the window he had made in the ark
and sent out a raven. It kept flying back and forth until the water had dried up from the earth.
Then Noah sent out a dove to see if the water had gone down from the surface of the ground.

But the dove could find nowhere to land, because there was still water over the whole earth. So it came back to Noah in the ark. He reached out his hand, took the dove and brought it back into the ark.
Noah waited seven more days, and then he sent the dove out of the ark again.
In the evening the dove came back to him, and there in its beak was a freshly picked olive leaf! Then Noah knew that the water had gone down from the earth.
He waited seven more days and sent the dove out again, but this time it did not come back to him.

By the first day of the first month of Noah's six hundred and first year, the water had dried up from the earth. Noah took the covering off the ark and looked out. He saw that the surface of the ground was dry.
By the twenty-seventh day of the second month, the earth was completely dry.
Then God said to Noah,
"Come out of the ark, you and your wife, and your sons and their wives.

Bring out every kind of living creature that is with you: the birds, the animals and all the creatures that move along the ground. Let them spread out over the earth, have many young and increase in number on it."
So Noah came out, together with his sons and his wife and his sons' wives.
All the animals, all the creatures that move along the ground and all the birds, everything that moves on the earth, came out of the ark, one kind after another.
Then Noah built an altar to the LORD. He took some of every kind of clean animal and clean bird, and he burned them on the altar as offerings to the LORD.

The LORD smelled the pleasing smell and said to himself, "I will never again curse the ground because of human beings, even though every plan of their hearts is evil from the time they are young. And I will never again destroy every living creature, as I have just done.
As long as the earth lasts, there will always be planting time and harvest time, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night."
